provenance: Second pass on the sexual register, correcting a coverage skew: the original file was half fruit-and-vegetable euphemism, which is the most famous slice of the vocabulary but a small one. This file covers the flirtation glyphs that are actually highest-frequency (🫦 👅 🤤 were absent entirely), shape- and pun-based euphemisms, act references, garment and setting cues, and the numeric construction. Descriptive reference in the same spirit as published platform trust-and-safety guidance; gated by default.

🫦.gloss: Added in Emoji 14.0 and adopted almost immediately as a flirtation marker. Higher-frequency in that role than most of the classic food euphemisms, which is why its absence from a euphemism list is a real gap.

👅.gloss: The tongue is the most direct non-food glyph in the register; also used non-sexually for cheek or mockery.

🤤.gloss: 'Drooling over' someone. Also applied entirely innocently to food, which is what makes it deniable.

🍈.gloss: 'Melons'. A long-standing English euphemism that predates emoji by decades.

🥜.gloss: 'Nuts'. Direct lexical carry-over from English slang.

🌰.gloss: A substitute for 🥜, used where that is filtered.

🥚.gloss: Splits between the anatomical euphemism and genuine conception and IVF discussion.

🕳️.gloss: Crude and unambiguous in context; the literal 'hole' reading survives mainly in gaming and hiking talk.

🍭.gloss: Licking-based euphemism, in the same family as 🍦.

🥕.gloss: A shape substitute for 🍆, useful precisely because it is less filtered.

🔩.gloss: 'Screw'. A pun on the object's name rather than its shape, which makes it opaque outside English.

🥄.gloss: Non-penetrative physical closeness; frequently affectionate rather than sexual.

🚿.gloss: Setting cue rather than an act reference.

🛋️.gloss: Contextual cue in the same family as 🛏️.

🏩.gloss: This is the *official* Unicode name. A specific Japanese institution — short-stay rooms rented by the hour — that most Western users read as a generic hotel or, because of the heart, a maternity ward.

🎈.gloss: Inflation-based euphemism, and a stand-in where no dedicated glyph exists.

🧴.gloss: The lotion bottle covers this by default because Unicode has no dedicated glyph; also used entirely literally for skincare.

💊.gloss: Two distinct sexual-health readings sitting alongside the recreational and literal-medication senses.

6️⃣9️⃣.gloss: A two-keycap construction rather than a single glyph. Also appears as a bare number in usernames and bios for the same joke.

💏.gloss: Officially just 'kiss'; ambiguous between romance and innuendo by design.

💑.gloss: Relationship-status marker more than an act reference.

✊.gloss: Only carries this reading paired with a phallic glyph; alone it is overwhelmingly solidarity or a fist bump.

🤏.gloss: The pinching hand as a size insult, quite separate from its 'a tiny amount' sense.

🌶️.gloss: Two unrelated sexual readings: a size insult in some cultures, and the 'spicy' content marker documented in the algospeak file.

📏.gloss: In dating bios a height disclosure; in flirtation, a different measurement.

🧎.gloss: Kneeling; overlaps heavily with the comedic-begging and devotional senses.

👙.gloss: Signals the kind of image rather than the garment; common in creator-account bios.

🩲.gloss: Added in Emoji 12.0 and used the same way as 👙.

💄.gloss: Marks a message as done-up and forward; also straightforwardly cosmetic.

🌊.gloss: A wave-based euphemism in the same family as 💦, considerably less common.

👀.gloss: Looking at something with interest or desire.

🍫.gloss: Used as a compliment about complexion in flirtation; read by many as fetishising rather than flattering.
